correctness.rationale: The original macroscopic equations (41)–(43) under equal rates/capacities and the stated normalization give the sum of the two separate crowding terms, with prey fractions x/(1+y) and xy/(1+y), and the stated predation and recruitment terms. At positive equilibria the predator equation forces λ=b/μ−1>0 and x=(1+y)/λ. The prey reaction on it is −P(y)/λ² with P=y²−By+1−λ and B=λ−aλ²/(1+λ). Root signs give the complete census: opposite signs for λ>1, the root 1−a/2 alongside zero at λ=1, and positive double or distinct roots precisely when B equals or exceeds 2√(1−λ) for 0<λ<1. The predator x-derivative G_x is positive along the positive nullcline, so det J=G_x P′/λ². This gives the lower saddle; the diagonal signs give negative trace and a sink at the upper root. The prey-only eigenvalues are −1 and μ(λ−1)/2. At the fold use r=x−(1+y)/λ as transverse coordinate: the second Jacobian column in (r,y) is zero, the trace is strictly negative, and a left zero eigenvector has nonzero first component since G_x>0. The reduced second derivative −2/λ² and a-derivative −y_f/(1+λ) project nontrivially, giving a generic fold. The rational witness follows by factoring P=(y−1/5)(y−1/2); the frozen standard-library checker and verification notes were inspected, not executed. These are homogeneous ODE results, not PDE stability or a global basin theorem.

value.rationale: The complete sharp classification is mathematically informative as a description of a motivated reaction law: it separates local failure of predator invasion from existence of a stable coexistence state and identifies the fold bounding that region. That structural value is already present in the covering theorem. The different rational witness alone is a routine illustration and supplies no valuable standalone repair.
